articleTitle: LTspice-model of thermoelectric Peltier-Seebeck element
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: A simple, symmetric, convertible into electric generator mode LTspice-model of Peltier-Seebeck element is proposed. The model parameters are extracted from the experimental measurement results of the electrical and thermal characteristics of the real elements.

articleTitle: Mathematical simulation of the chaotic oscillator based on a field-effect transistor structure with negative resistance
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: In this paper a classical circuit of the Kiyashko-Pikovsky-Rabinovich deterministic chaos oscillator based on a field-effect transistor structure with negative resistance got the further development. The chaotic oscillation dynamic processes in this oscillator have been researched using the improved model. Phase portraits of the oscillator in different operating modes have been obtained.

articleTitle: Switch operation power losses of quasi-resonant pulse converter with parallel resonant circuit
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The analysis of electromagnetic processes in power switch of a zero-current switching quasi-resonant pulse converter with parallel resonant circuit is presented in this paper. The analysis performed by stitching equations illustrating change of power switch current and power switch voltage. The obtained results for each switching interval allowed to estimate the overall power dissipation and power losses for all switching intervals.

articleTitle: The effect of load power factor on the efficiency of three-phase four-wire power system with shunt active filter
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The formula for determining efficiency of three-phase four-wire power system for unbalanced non-sinusoidal mode with a given load power factor and the known ratio of short circuit power to load active power has been derived. The new formula of the apparent power, which takes into account the power losses of the neutral conductor, has been used in order to determine the power factor. The adequacy of the proposed ratios is shown in the example of calculation of efficiency of three-phase four-wire power system for a simple unbalanced load. Analytical condition for the energy feasibility of a shunt active power filter (SAF) to improve the efficiency of the power system has been derived.

articleTitle: The pressure transducer based on the dual-mode piezoresonant sensors with modulated interelectrode gap
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This paper represents the principles of the dual-mode pressure transducers based on the piezoresonant sensors with modulated interelectrode gap, considers the experimental study results of the characteristics of piezoresonant pressure transducer based on quartz crystal, which is excited at the basic and additional (anharmonic) modes of oscillation.

articleTitle: Modification of materials surface layers by low-energy ion irradiation in glow discharge
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Possibility of increase of welded connections reliability in the electronic devices elements consisting of the materials, which vary by mechanical, physical and chemical properties and have a limited or unsatisfactory weldability, is considered. It is shown, that prior modification of a chemical composition of metal-environment interface by method of introduction of recoil atoms from the sputtered thin metal films in the glow discharge at energy of ions to 1 keV make an effective impact on diffusion processes of solid-state welding of metals by pressure and elevate connection durability on 20 … 40%.

articleTitle: Bio-inspired plastic controller for a robot arm to shake hand with human
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The future coexistence of humanoid robots and human being presuppose knowledge of cognitive mechanisms involved in interpersonal human physical and social interactions. The act of a handshake is an example of a physical interpersonal interaction that plays an important social role because it is based on physical and social couplings that lead to synchronization of motion. Studying handshake for robotics is interesting as it can expand the behavioral properties of robots for interaction with a human being in a more natural way. Previous experiments have shown that the phase of physical contact which contains hands tightening initiates a phenomenon of mutual synchrony. Considering the biological rhythmic nature of handshake phenomenon, a robot controller inspired by rhythmic structures of the human motor nervous system is proposed in this paper. The model is based on coupled rhythmic neurons, constituting a central pattern generator with learning mechanisms for the frequency of the movement perceived during the interaction. Experiments with a robot arm show that it is possible for the robot to learn to synchronize its rhythm with the human rhythms imposed during the handshake.

articleTitle: The computation of line spectral frequencies using discrete wavelet transform for electrocardiograms processing
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: An approach for glucose meters was improved. We process electrocardiograms of patients to detect change of glucose concentration in the blood. The technique uses discrete wavelet transform for electrocardiograms processing. Standard oral glucose tolerance test used to check fifty six patients complains of type 2 diabetes symptoms. The square of the Matthews correlation coefficient 0.93 has been achieved on examination.

articleTitle: Simulation and synthesis of networks-on-chip by using NoCSimp HDL library
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This paper proposes an approach to the synthesis and modeling of networks-on-chip (NoCs) by using the NoCSimp library based on a simplified wormhole router with central buffer and without virtual channels. The analysis of the results of simulation and synthesis of NoCs with regular and quasi-optimal topologies with number of nodes 8 and 9 is given. It is shown that in the case where the number of NoC nodes is not a power of 2 the use of quasi-optimal topologies offers a significant advantage.

articleTitle: Signal processing in MEMS inertial measurement units for dynamic motional control
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: We examine statistical models of noise, processing calculus, filtering and signal processing in MEMS-technology inertial measurement units (IMUs). Dynamic systems are controlled using the measured data which perturbed by the noise, drift, bias, etc. In aerospace, automotive, electronic, manufacturing, medical, naval and robotic systems, the linear (ax, ay, az) and angular (αθαφαψ) accelerations are measured as (âx,ây,âz) and (αθ, αφ, αψ). The major objective is to enable physical and processing data integrity (conformity, consistency, completeness and validity) to assess system performance and capabilities by deriving adequate post-processed (ãx, ãy,ãz) and (αθ, αφ, αθ, αψ). Low-power multi-degree-of-freedom MEMS accelerometers and gyroscopes are studied. These IMUs include multi-axis accelerometer and gyroscope with processing integrated circuits (ICs). These ICs implement sensing, diagnostics, compensation, interfacing, conversions, signal conditioning, etc. The strategic-, navigation-, tactical- and consumer-grade IMUs may require post-processing. The data integrity enhancement is needed in the inertial navigation systems (aircraft, satellites, submarines and unmanned aerial vehicles), cell phones, gimbals, robots, etc. Noise attenuation, ~arcsecond/sec and ~μg stability, ~500 Hz bandwidth, linearity, and adequate signal processing may be accomplished by the navigation-grade IMUs. This will reduce the dependence on global positioning systems, as well as ensure uncompromised navigation, guidance and control. The information quality is affected by the device physics, probabilistic characteristics, processing capabilities, etc. The data quality affects system's performance metrics, decision analysis, mission effectiveness, etc. The MEMS IMUs characteristics are of a particular importance for command, control and intelligence systems. With fundamental limits on sensing, microfabrication and microelectronics constraints, the advanced processing calculus and enabling signal processing may ensure beyond-state-of-the-art capabilities.

articleTitle: Optimization of NDR VCOs for microwave applications
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: In this paper we present a comparison of five proposed negative-differential resistance (NDR) voltage controlled oscillators (VCOs) for microwave applications. The VCO circuits comprise a GaAs transistor and a BJT current mirror (CM). The equation for calculating the terminal current is derived for each oscillator circuit. The comparison of VCOs is conducted by using a commonly used figure of merit (FOM). The best designed VCO is tuned in a frequency band of 1.252 to 1.595 GHz with maximum phase-noise of −142.3 dBc/Hz@100-kHz and delivers minimum 19.2 dBm of output power. Power consumption of the VCO core is 52 mW. The implemented prototype of the oscillator operates at 683.8 MHz, draws 2.1 mA from a 9 V power supply and generates low-noise low-distortion signal.

articleTitle: Electrical sintering of inkjet printed sensor structures on plyimide substrate
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Inkjet printing of Ag-nanoparticle dispersions was used to fabricate strain sensors on polyimide substrate. Two sintering methods i.e. conventional thermal and electrical sintering has been examined and compared regarding obtained strain gauge characteristics. Gauge factors of around 2.9 (after conventional thermal sintering) and 2.6 (after rapid electrical sintering) have been obtained. Due to the electric sintering a significant reduction of the processing time (< 5 seconds) can be achieved.

articleTitle: Local electronic properties of the surface of the nanostructured silicon layers
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Local energy characteristics of nanostructured silicon surface were studied by the tunneling spectroscopy method. Obtained current-voltage characteristics of nanostructured silicon layers, depending on the parameters of the formation of nanostructured silicon, without and under the illumination by ultraviolet radiation on air and in gas environment. Thus there is a different degree of filling of the valence band and the conduction band, a significant difference in the bandgap and the appearance on the curve of tunneling conductance of new peaks in gas environment. The results indicate that the method of scanning tunneling spectroscopy can be used in the field of surface chemistry, nanoelectronics and sensors.

articleTitle: Fuzzy computer-aided diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease using MRI and PET statistical features
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: In this paper, MRI and PET image features from selected brain regions are used as inputs in a fuzzy inference classification system for automatic diagnosis of Alzheimer's Disease (AD). Mean values of voxel intensity in spatial regions of interest which are extracted from normalized MRI and PET scans of brain gray matter were used as features. Area under receiver operating characteristic (AUC) was used as a classification performance measure, being function of the number of brain anatomical and functional regions of interest from which the features were extracted. In the result, combination of features from 7 MRI regions and 39 PET regions gave the highest performance of classification (AUC=0.94).

articleTitle: Sigma-delta modulators transfer functions derivation
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Sigma-delta modulator structure is presented in the form of matrix equations. The equations allow to easily obtain analytical expressions for the noise and signal transfer functions for arbitrary modulator structures. As a result the modulator structures analysis and comparison become straightforward.

articleTitle: Light absorption of nanocomposite thin films
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Absorption profiles of thin films with gold spheroidal nanoinclusions are calculated in the framework of a local-field approach. The dependence of the absorption spectra is obtained on the volume fraction, the shape of inclusions and their orientation relative to the normal to the film surface for probing monochromatic beams of s and p-polarizations under irradiating the film at different angles. The possibility of a controlled impact on the optical properties of nanocomposite films and using the special thin nanocomposite films as an anti-reflective coating in solar cells are discussed.

articleTitle: Simulation the behavior of robot sub-swarm in spatial corridors
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The article presents simulation of the robot swarm behavior, taking into consideration the model of robots dividing into sub-swarms to perform similar tasks within a limited spatial corridor. To avoid robots crashing with each other, the authors propose to use the three-dimensional (3D) bodies (sphere) instead of spatial points in the traveling salesman problem (TSP) solution. For simplifying the solution of such problem, it is proposed to solve 3D problem via concatenation of solving two 2D problems of moving sphere, as "salesmen" move in planes, limiting the spatial corridors. The sphere in this case moves on the vertical plane notwithstanding the spatial corridors. The proposed simulation model of the swarm robots behavior is described as dynamic smart system.

articleTitle: Application of higher-order spectral analysis to lung sounds in patients with chronic bronchitis
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This article describes a method that allows to classify lung sounds by the category of healthy patient and patient with bronchitis. The method is based on the use of apparatus of higher-order statistics, namely on calculating of skewness and kurtosis coefficients, as well as the calculation and graphing parametric bispectrum. In addition, the calculation of parametric bispectrum applied to separate phases of respiration. It allowed determining what specific phases contained some breathing artifacts which indicates the pathology.

articleTitle: Location prediction approach for context-aware energy management system
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Given that over the past few decades energy demand has been continuously increasing and the context-aware energy management systems for renewable sources and electrical loads have become much more sophisticated, the paper presents the application of location prediction methods in such systems. CAEMSs are highly distributed, can manage large amounts of energy-related data and have to be able to react rapidly and intelligently when conditions change, leading to real-time challenges. We address one of the most valuable context prediction tasks — learning human habits and behavioral patterns for indoor location prediction. The motivation behind choosing this problem is that knowledge of the location, presumably entered by the user, can initiate several preparation routines to maximize comfort and minimize energy consumption. Automatic adjustment of light or temperature, by heating rooms prior to their occupation, can be stated as an example of such a routine.

articleTitle: Diffusion bonding technique concerning production of microchannel heat exchangers
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Diffusion bonding process of aluminium 1070A concerning production of microchannel heat exchangers (MCHE) has been investigated. It has been proposed to raise manufacturability of the process owing to introduction into contact zone of joining details composition on the basis of sodium silicate before welding. The results of investigations of microstructure and chemical composition of welded joints and also mechanical strength of products have been presented.

articleTitle: About the impact of informative features selection in the mutually orthogonal decompositions of biomedical signals for their recognition
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The estimation issues of features' informativity in portraits of biomedical signals during their mutually orthogonal decompositions in recognition systems with supervised learning and the technology of revealing and the implementation of reserves of improving the probability of correct pattern recognition by reducing the uninformative features from their portraits are being considered. The content and impact of the proposed technology for the given signals' decomposition are being illustrated by the test case in the application to the task of QRS-complexes types' recognition, suitable in the current study by the availability of existing data for recognition system training.

articleTitle: Structure imperfection and dielectric properties of single-phase multifferoic Bi1-xLaxFeO3-δ
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Using the rapid liquid sintering method the samples of multiferroic Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>La<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>FeO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-δ</sub> (x = 0, 0.1, 0.3 and 0.5) were obtained. Their structure and dielectric properties were investigated. The X-ray diffraction, thermogravimetric, scanning electron microscopy and dielectric spectroscopy methods were used. The molar formulas of defective structure Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>La<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>FeO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-δ</sub> were defined. An analysis of the frequency dependence of the relative permittivity ε(f) and dielectric loss tangent tanδ (f) at the low frequency (f = 1...10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> Hz) and microwave (f = 8...12 GHz) bands was conducted. It was established that the Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.9</sub>La<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.1</sub>FeO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> composition has the greatest value of dielectric permittivity.

articleTitle: A new intelligence-based approach for rhinomanometric data processing
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Aerodynamic characteristics of nasal airflow are important for obstruction problems detection. In clinical practice, we analyze behavior of hydrodynamic resistance coefficient. This paper proposes a component of real-time automated system for rhinomanometric measurements. The component is a real-time alert to help users define a correct measurement.

articleTitle: Dimensional dependencies of optical parameters of nanodimensional metal particles
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The results of researches of the investigations of dimensional dependencies of optical parameters of nanodimensional particles of silver, nickel chrome in high-frequency spectral diapason 1.1+3.2 eV are presented. It is shown, that values of high-frequency conductivity of nanodimensional particles of these metals are considerable lesser than in macroscopic samples and with diminishing of particle dimensions the values of high-frequency conductivity diminish by 1-2 orders. Determined is the connection of dimensional changes of high-frequency conductivity of nanoparticles with their specific absorption.

articleTitle: Measurement of slice thickness in digital tomosynthesis and digital laminography
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Experimental comparison of slice thickness obtained by medical digital X-ray laminography and general purpose digital tomosynthesis was carried out using a specially made phantom. Theoretical estimation of slice thickness in case of filtered backprojection reconstruction is proposed. Estimation has good agreement with the experimental results.

articleTitle: Increasing the resistance of computer systems towards virus attacks
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: A concept of the computer system with resistance towards virus attacks on the basis of hardware was proposed. The structure of antivirus protection system was designed. Neural immune detectors for the identification and classification of virus attacks are implemented on programmable logic arrays. Mamdani fuzzy inference rules were proposed to use in order to make decisions on providing counteraction methods against virus attacks.

articleTitle: Investigation of native oxide removing from HCPA ALD grown GaN thin films surface utilizing HF solutions
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The paper consider oxygen contamination of HCPA ALD grown GaN films under an air conditioning and during different time duration. High resolution XPS analysis of HCPA ALD grown GaN films after diluted 1:10 HF(41 %): H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O and undiluted HF (41 %) influence on oxygen impurities was investigated. Lesser oxygen impurities have been observed. Better resistivity to oxygen atoms of GaN thin films after diluted HF solution treatment was achieved compared to undiluted HF treatment and without treatment.

articleTitle: Influence of process time on ZnO and ZnO:Al nanorods formation
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The original results of ZnO and Al-doped ZnO nanorods formation by hydrothermal method on the 128YX-cut lithium niobate and silicon substrates with synthesized seed-layer by sol-gel technique were presented. The influence of process time on morphometric parameters of synthesized nanorods was investigated using scanning electron microscopy. It was ascertained that the length and diameter of the ZnO nanorods increased from 150±10 nm and 55±5 nm to 530±80 nm and 75±20 nm respectively when the process time was increased from 30 min to 120 min for ZnO nanorods on the 128YX-cut lithium niobate substrates. The diameter of Al-doped ZnO nanorods increased from 50±10 nm to 75±15 nm with process time increasing from 30 min to 60 min for samples on silicon substrates. These results could be used for the synthesis of ZnO and Al-doped ZnO nanorods with required morphometric properties on single crystal substrates in development and manufacturing of advanced electronic devices as well as nanoscale devices.

articleTitle: H2O2 and alcohol sensors on porous silicon
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: In the paper simple Me/por-Si/Me structures are used as hydrogen peroxide and alcohol sensors with sensitivity up to 3 μA/% and 5.3 μA/% respectively. It was shown that depending on formation conditions porous silicon layer formed in different etching solutions can be selective between two substances.

articleTitle: Modeling of the elastic properties of the core-shell Au-Ag nanorod
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Mechanical properties of the core-shell Au-Ag nanorod were studied within classical molecular dynamic simulation technique. Strain-stress curves were calculated for both tension and compression. The values of the Young modulus were estimated from elastic part of strain-stress dependencies. It is shown that Au-Ag nanorod preserves core-shell structure during the deformation process in the central region of the sample.

articleTitle: Specifics of the X7R capacitors application in the high frequency inverters
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The high energy density X7R multilayer ceramic capacitors are widely used in the power electronic circuitries. Those capacitors are characterized by high nominal capacitance, voltage and low equivalent series resistance ESR. The latter may become critical in case of the high current, high frequency application and may cause a temperature rise significantly exceeding one estimated using ESR value from the datasheet. This behavior may be traced to the induced piezoelectric effect and resulting electromechanical resonances and losses. This article presents test results correcting X7R capacitance dependency on the bias voltage and multiple resonance dependency of ESR on the frequency and DC bias which may be useful for mitigating the excessive heating of the capacitors.

articleTitle: Spectrum analysis of a bipolar voltage on basis the double Fourier series
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Necessity of bipolar voltage modulation using in inverters with transformers are shown. Analysis voltage spectrum with bipolar modulation on basis double Fourier series are proposed. Two different cases depending of multiplicity parameter are described. Spectrum characteristic of bipolar modulation are analyzed.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic engineering of a plasmonic-strip loaded quantum wire
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: We consider the two-dimensional (2D) problem of the H-polarized electromagnetic eigenmodes of a silver nanostrip placed in the centre of an active shell in the form of circular quantum wire (QW). Both the lasing mode frequency and the associated threshold value of material gain in QW, needed to bring the mode to the light emission, are extracted from the lasing eigenvalue problem (LEP). Such nanostrip-based laser can emit visible light on several localized surface plasmon (LSP) modes and also on the "shell modes" or QW polariton modes perturbed by the strip. We present numerical results on the mode threshold gain dependences on the radius of the active shell.

articleTitle: Design of edge boosting digital control circuit for high-speed ICs
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This paper presents an edge boosting method for I/O output buffer using signal front detection digital control circuit. The presented architecture detects I/O data or clock signal transitions and activates additional drive strength fingers in the output buffer resulting in output current increase which improves the slew rate, compensating for losses in transmission lines. The presented edge boosting method can be used in the I/O circuits of such standards as DDR(Double Data Rate), USB(Universal Serial Bus), PCI(Peripheral Component Interconnect) etc.

articleTitle: MR image reconstruction from data acquired on an irregular k-space trajectory
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The reconstruction for the magnetic resonance imaging under condition of using irregular measured signal data array for reconstructing of the spine density spatial distribution are offered. For experimentally measured data using a Fourier-Zymography in Magnetic Resonance Imaging techniques simulated the received signal and realised the reverse reconstruction of tomograms. The evaluation of the quality of tomograms with incomplete signal data set has been carried out.

articleTitle: Atrial electrical activity extraction for atrial fibrillation assessment
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The work is dedicated to noninvasive research of atrial electrical activity by its extraction from the surface electrocardiogram recordings and spectral and time-frequency analysis for fibrillatory frequency detection and tracking. Atrial electrical activity and ventricular activity were separated from real multichannel recordings with symptoms of atrial fibrillation by means of independent component analysis. To identify the source that corresponds to atrial electrical activity the frequency spectrums and coefficients of skewness and kurtosis were determined. Also atrial activity extraction was performed by average beat subtraction method. The comparison of obtained results was carried out. Spectral analysis by Fast Fourier Transform and Multiple Signal Classification methods as well as time-frequency analysis were used to find and track dominant atrial fibrillation frequency.

articleTitle: Error correction technique based on modular correcting codes
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The paper presents a technique for error correction based on modular correcting codes, providing error correction in two information symbols using a single control character. The algorithms of error detection and correction and decoder structure have been developed. The proposed technique of detecting errors based on modular correcting codes is characterized by a lower surplus in comparison with the previously developed modular correcting codes.

articleTitle: Bioimpedance monitoring of dialysis patients during ultrafiltration
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: In this article the features of the developed device for bioimpedance analysis with an active electrodes and the results of its verification during ultrafiltration in the hemodialysis are described. The correlation between bioimpedance on 20 and 500 kHz frequencies with a profile and speed of ultrafiltration during hemodialysis is illustrated. The aim of the experiment was to determine the possibility of using the device for bioimpedance analysis to assess the dry weight of the patient and to monitoring of his functional state during the procedure.

articleTitle: Peculiarities of lossy compression of optical and medical images corrupted by noise
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Lossy compression is often used in practice of image processing. A specific feature of our research is that we assume optical and/or medical images to be compressed noisy and take this fact into account. Moreover, major attention is paid to the specific case of spatially correlated noise. The study is carried out for five different compression methods based on discrete cosine and wavelet orthogonal transforms. It is shown that for all these techniques the existence of optimal operation point (OOP) is possible according to standard and visual quality metrics. Peculiarities of dependences of these metrics on parameters that control compression are analyzed. It is demonstrated that noise intensity and correlation properties influence behavior of these dependences. Some practical recommendations are given.

articleTitle: Parameters identification of injection plastic moulding heaters
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Predefined heater parameters are involved in self-tuned temperature control for plastic moulding. However the heater system transfer function depends on many external parameters, such as barrel filling level, type of plastic etc. This paper discusses a recursive least-square estimation of plastic moulding heater parameters identification. The real heaters have been estimated by recursive least-square method as 2nd or 3rd order transfer function having an error less than 7.5%. The optimal sampling time for the identification process of different heater cartridges has been obtained from Matlab simulation. The parameters of estimated model can be used in self-tuned temperature controllers for injection plastic moulding heater.

articleTitle: Sensitivity of automatic speech recognition to excessive noise and late reverberation reduction
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Noise and late reverberation reduction algorithms were studied using objective speech quality and speech recognition accuracy (Acc%) measures. Negative consequences of excessive noise and late reverberation reduction for automatic speech recognition had been demonstrated. Study of speech quality measures showed that only few of them were in good agreement with Acc%. It was shown that Acc% may be in creased by means of proper choice of a priory signal-to-noise assessment technique.

articleTitle: Filter realization technique based on gyrator-resonator circuit replacement
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The application of active elements such as gyrator and negative capacitance simulator in conjunction with piezoelectric resonators allows to imitate simple LC circuits employed in bandpass, low-pass and high-pass filter design. In contrast to the circuits composed of distributed elements, active circuits with resonators provide minimal sensitivity to component variations and less parameter offsets during production. They also have smaller dimensions and can be integrated with digital signal processing on a single chip including the possibility electronic adjustment. The replacement principle of LC circuit prototypes by the active analogs is described in details. The active low-pass filter was designed and analyzed using the presented approach to review the special considerations about resonators application.

articleTitle: Transmission coefficients for the cone-beam tomography
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: In this article are investigated the transmission coefficients of aluminum and water. It was found that transmission coefficients calculated by the image intensifying screen brightness and by the doses are differed. It is shown that the correction transmission coefficients can be implemented by using corrective coefficients and hardware. It is experimentally found that the addition in the X-tract of the aluminum filter by corresponding size make small difference between the transmission coefficients, calculated by the image intensifying screen brightness and the doses measured by dosimeter.

articleTitle: Formation of the diagnostic HR ECG features of post-traumatic myocardial dystrophy
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This research is aimed at identifying and estimating of high resolution electrocardiography (HR ECG) features of the heart disorders after an extreme impact on the human organism due to the combat mine blast injury. The study of healthy and injured patients' HR ECG signals was done in the research. The diagnostic features of the post-traumatic myocardial dystrophy based on the principal component analysis (PCA) are suggested.

articleTitle: A novel approach for process variation detection
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: A novel approach for process variation detection (PVD) is proposed. Named "dynamic measurement", the proposed method is able to detect process corner type. Information on process variability is represented in digital signal (code). Use of such approach can exclude necessity of use of special measurement equipment or embedded test structures (ring oscillators, transistor arrays, etc.) during testing, thereby minimizing process variability evaluation time and cost. The proposed approach can further be improved for more detailed information on process corner/variation. In this paper, metal-oxide-semiconductor (MOS) current-voltage characteristics are used to design a circuit based on the proposed approach. With the aid of this approach one can detect not only parameter variations of n or p-type transistors, but also their combinations, resistors, transistors with short channels.

articleTitle: Transient transformation of surface plasmon due to time variations in dielectric permittivity of nanowire environment
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: In this paper, a 2D problem of a surface plasmon transformation due to a time variation of silver nanowire environment is analytically solved. Solution of the problem is derived in the form of the Laplace transform. Accurate time domain inversion makes it possible to analyze transient and steady state regimes.

articleTitle: Size effect influence on the electronic properties of Ge2Sb2Te5 films prepared by ion plasma sputtering
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Physical and chemical criteria for ion plasma deposition of chalcogenide glass nano-films have been studied. Research results demonstrate structure, temperature dependences and electrical conductivity data of nanoscaled Ge<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Sb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Te<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub> films. Thin films were obtained by ion-plasma sputtering with thickness from 25 to 175 nm. Scanning and Transmission Electron Microscopy images revealed amorphous and homogeneous film structure. Temperature dependence of films electrical conductivity investigation was performed. It has been shown that with decreasing film thickness the conductivity decreases and the activation energy of conductivity increases. It has been found from studies of the current-voltage Ge2Sb2Te5 film characteristics reversible switching effect caused by a reversible phase transformation "amorphous ↔polycristalline state" takes place. The threshold voltage Uth and switching time tsw with decreasing film thickness were reduced significantly.

articleTitle: Fano-shape grating resonances of 3D infinite double-periodic grating of thin dielectric bricks
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: We study the plane wave scattering from double periodic dielectric layer located in free space and illuminated by a linearly polarized plane wave. For the problem solution, we use the method of integral functional based on the vector volume integral-differential equations for the equivalent electric and magnetic polarization currents of the assumed periodic medium. Reflectance and transmittance as a function of the normalized wavelength and the grating parameters are analyzed. Extraordinary sharp grating-type resonances are revealed in the TM- and TE-polarized wave scattering near but not equal to the Rayleigh wavelengths of non-zero diffraction orders.

articleTitle: Effect of substrate temperature and Ga source precursor on growth and material properties of GaN grown by hollow cathode plasma assisted atomic layer deposition
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: GaN thin films grown by hollow cathode plasma-assisted atomic layer deposition (HCPA-ALD) at two different substrate temperatures (250 and 450 °C) are compared. Effect of two different Ga source materials named as trimethylgallium (TMG) and triethylgallium (TEG) on GaN growth and film quality is also investigated and reviewed. Films were characterized by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, spectroscopic ellipsometery, and grazing incidence X-ray diffraction. GaN film deposited by TMG revealed better structural, chemical, and optical properties in comparison with GaN film grown with TEG precursor. When compared on basis of different substrate temperature, GaN films grown at higher substrate temperature revealed better structural and optical properties.

articleTitle: Tunability limits of the microstrip line with electromechanical control
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The paper presents study of the tunable microstrip line with electromechanical control. The study derives dependencies of the effective permittivity and insertion loss on combination of substrate material properties and device dimensions. Asymptotic boundaries for effective permittivity and loss are derived.

articleTitle: Components of micro- and nanoelectronics based on silicon structures for cryogenic temperatures
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The paper deals with the solution of scientific and applied problems of development of elements of sensing equipment on the basis of silicon-on-insulator structures (SOI) doped with boron impurities. The paper presents the impedance measurements of electrical properties of polycrystalline silicon films (with concentration ranged from 2.4×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> to 1.7×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>) in the silicon-on-insulator structures obtained in the temperature range 4.2-70K in the frequency range from 10Hz to 250kHz as well as checking a possibility of their use as components of solid state electronics efficient at cryogenic temperatures. Based on silicon-on-insulator structures the discrete solid state elements (inductive, capacitive elements) and combined elements (oscillatory circuits) implemented by positioning technologies were developed. To design the oscillatory circuit a combination of two elements consisting of SOI-structure with a dopant concentration corresponding to the dielectric and metal side of metal-insulator transition (obtaining by double diffusion of boron impurities in polysilicon) was used.

articleTitle: An optimal degree approximation of the surface control for photovoltaic maximum power point tracking system
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: A new method to estimate a position of PV maximum power point based on universal approximation of experimental data as a function of temperature and irradiance has been represented in the paper. An optimal polynomial degree for the proposed correction function of universal approximation has been found. The control surface for industrial KVAZAR KV-250M PV panel has been obtained by numerical analysis. Relative tolerance of the proposed method is less then 1.6% in the operation range of temperature and irradiance and not exceeds 6.3% outside the range of PV reasonable use. The obtained control surface can be used in ANFIS controller design for PV maximum power point tracking.

articleTitle: Power electronics, microelectronics and propulsion systems for solar-powered unmanned aerial vehicles
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: We examine power and energy systems for propulsion, guidance, navigation, control, communication and other primary, secondary and auxiliary systems of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The major objective is to develop a scalable and modular design concept in energy harvesting, energy storage and energy management. Different energy sources, including solar energy, are used to power light-weight long-endurance low-, medium- and high-altitude UAVs, satellites and other platforms. Fixed wing UAVs must ensure flight specifications, mission effectiveness, speed, altitude, endurance, etc. Agile and maneuverable rotary wing UAVs are also enabled by alternative energy sources. We study high-efficiency energy systems, low-power electronics and energy management for propulsion systems, control surfaces actuators, sensors and other key components.

articleTitle: Influence of topological parameters of MEMS-enabled tunable microstrip resonators on their characteristics
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Article is devoted to the resonant elements topological parameters optimization for maximum resonance frequency tuning efficiency. Stub and ring resonators based on microstrip lines are presented. The maximum length of the movable stub resonator part with micromechanical tuning was determined. Criteria for optimal ring resonator width were obtained. Such recommendations for stub and ring resonators increasing the maximum frequency tuning limit and allowing to avoid distortion in resonator's transmission coefficient.

articleTitle: Nanotechnology for portable energy systems: Modular photovoltaics, energy storage and electronics
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: For portable energy systems, this paper examines nanotechnology-enabled high-power and high-energy density microelectronics, power electronics, energy sources, and energy storage solutions. These energy systems are used in various applications including aerospace, biomedical, communication, electronics, micro-electromechanical systems (MEMS), robotics, etc. Proof-of-concept autonomous power systems are designed, and, practical solutions are substantiated and proposed. We perform applied research and technology developments in the design of efficient energy harvesting, energy management, and energy storage systems. To guarantee modularity and compatibility, the following components and modules are examined: (1) Low-power microelectronics; (2) High-power-density power electronics with high-current, high-voltage and high-frequency power MOSFETs; (3) High-efficiency energy harvesting sources such as solar cells and electromagnetic generators; (4) High specific energy and power density electrochemical energy storage devices; (5) Optimal energy management systems. The most advanced technology-proven nanoscale microelectronics, MEMS sensors, and energy conversion solutions are studied. The modular design, enabling topologies and optimization schemes result in high-performance micro- and mini-scale energy systems.

articleTitle: Optical properties of a dielectric slab front-loaded with a grating of plasmonic silver nanowires
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The electromagnetic properties of a circular silver nanowire grating placed over a dielectric slab are investigated using the Maxwell formalism. The scattering properties are analyzed for the normally incident H-polarized plane wave. The lasing properties are studied for the same configuration however the dielectric slab refractive index is assumed having a negative imaginary part. The lasing modes are compared in terms of the lasing thresholds.

articleTitle: Dose reduction and object measuring in stereo X-ray systems
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: X-Ray stereo imaging is a promising medical imaging modality, offering 3D observational patient tissue at significantly lower doses than computed tomography or tomosynthesis. Decrease of patient dose arises from the fact that only two images are necessary to create the stereo image. Nevertheless, the ability to measure the distance in stereoscopic X-Ray scene still remains not elaborated. This paper experimentally demonstrates the method for measuring the dimensions of the geometrical object from the X-Ray stereo and shows the possibility to get a stereo image at patient dose lower than two single X-Ray images.

articleTitle: Generation of short THz pulses due to modulation instability in waveguides with SrTiO3 paraelectric
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: It is investigated the modulation instability of transversely bounded long THz pulses in waveguides on the base of the paraelectric SrTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> at the temperatures 77 K. The cubic nonlinearity and the frequency dispersion correspond to existence of envelope solitons and the modulation instability of long input pulses, whereas in the transverse direction the instability is absent. There exists a possibility to generate the regular sequences of short THz pulses due to the modulation instability in the waveguides with SrTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>. The focusing of input long pulses reduces the threshold of modulation instability at relatively low frequencies. At higher frequencies near the soft mode frequency the regular sequence of pulses can be generated in the waveguides with optimum widths.

articleTitle: Data processing analysis in nano-and microelectronics processing platforms
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Recent progress in nanotechnologies and pervasive concepts of microelectronics encompass to advance semiconductor devices, front-end processes, molecular engineering paradigms and high-performance processing platforms. The technology-centric design and new processing paradigms are deployed and commercialized in enabled-functionality systems. New practical concepts are needed to ensure real-time functional verification, validation, failure analysis, identification and detection to enable failure-tolerance and error-correction. We report and apply a concept to derive information estimates, and, measure data processing quantities in microelectronic devices.

articleTitle: On chip resistance value compensation technique for termination resistor
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: In this paper a new approach for on chip compensation of resistor value which can change due to process and temperature variations is presented. There is a special circuit which generates three bits for compensation corresponding to the variation of termination resistor value. The generated bits connect compensation resistors to termination resistor in parallel and in series through demultiplexor according to the generated bits.

articleTitle: 3-D modeling of frequency spectrum of volume spherical resonator by using FDTD method
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: We present the use of FDTD method to obtain the resonant frequencies of a volume 3D spherical microwave resonator for further its analyses and modeling in quantum (wave) chaos problem. Because a spherical cavity resonator can be considered as billiard dynamical system, studying frequency resonator spectrum and its changes under the influence of inhomogeneties inside of the resonator allows us to detect wave chaos.

articleTitle: Anomalous dependence of carbon nanotubes work function on humidity
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The impact of humidity on the single- and multi-walled carbon nanotubes field emission characteristics, such as work function and emission current, was studied. The behavior of carbon nanotubes on Si, Al, stainless steel and polyethylene naphthalate substrates during humidity changing was compared with pristine metals and other materials without nanotubes. Work function of the samples was measured in ambient conditions and in humidity range of 25-100 %. The strong correlation between work function and humidity of carbon nanotubes was found and strong anticorrelation was observed for control samples without CNT.

articleTitle: The interaction between constant magnetic field and magnetic nanopartricles in human tissue mimicking phantom
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The article describes a study of the interaction between constant magnetic field and magnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (NP) in human tissue mimicking breast phantom with tumor. The presence of phantom without NP reduces the intensity of the magnetic field by 40% as opposed when NP located into phantom the intensity of the magnetic field increases approximately by 20%. The dependence between constant magnetic field and ferromagnetic NP is well described by physical model. Thus, during use of constant magnetic field necessary personalize magnetic parameters in technology of magnetic antitumor therapy.

articleTitle: Highly regular LIPSS on silicon decorated with gold nanoparticles for plasmonic applications
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Plasmonic properties of gold nanoparticles self-assembled on silicon surfaces are significantly enhanced by a periodic surface ripples induced by ultrashort laser pulses. The nanostructured surfaces open new perspectives for production of photonic and plasmonic-sensor elements.

articleTitle: Feedback modelling using voltage or current divider
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: A technique is developed for transformation of any of four possible configurations of feedback systems: parallel-parallel, parallel-series, series-parallel, and series-series, into a voltage or current divider. Several examples are given to illustrate the application of the developed technique.

articleTitle: Analysis of high-performance DC-DC switching converters
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This paper examines high-performance dc-dc high switching frequency converters. Enabling topologies are examined. Passive soft switching schemes are studied to increase efficiency, minimize losses, reduce stresses, increase power density, ensure energy recovery, increase switching frequency, reduce electromagnetic interference, etc. Analog control algorithms are designed and implemented. The experimental results show optimal or near-optimal performance. The output voltage stabilization and accurate voltage tracking may be ensured with zero steady-state error. Our technology-centric solutions and findings are analytically and experimentally substantiated.

articleTitle: Electron heating during intervalley scattering
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: A mathematical modeling and simulation of the electron gas heating in multi-valley semiconductors of the AIHBV type are presented in the paper. The expressions for the rate of the energy relaxation on intervalley transitions can be used in design processes. Proposed equations differ from the usual expressions by additional terms, one of which depends on intervalley distance.

articleTitle: Thermal stability of shielded cylindrical metal-dielectric resonator
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The research of the thermal stability of the composite shielded cylindrical metal-dielectric resonator was performed. The sensitivities of resonant frequency to changes of resonator parameters are shown. The resulting temperature coefficient of resonant frequency is analyzed.

articleTitle: Development of nc-Si based intrinsic layer for HIT solar cells by ion-beam sputtering
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: In this paper the method of ion-beam sputtering was applied to produce nanocrystalline silicon (nc-Si) for emitter and intrinsic layers. Nanocrystalline silicon is more stable over time by reducing the degradation under the Staebler-Wronski effect than amorphous silicon. Reduction of surface recombination on the interface between "c-Si/nc-Si" was achieved by forming of nanocrystalline silicon via the ion-beam sputtering.

articleTitle: Capacitor mismatch correction method in pipeline ADCs
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Capacitor mismatch correction method for Pipeline ADC is presented in this paper. The proposed architecture allows getting identical capacitors over PVT, which is needed to increase noise immunity and accuracy of ADC. Noise immunity of ADC is important parameter. ADCs which are used in communication systems needed high nose immunity to avoid data error. The proposed method also allows designing ADCs with high resolution, because allowed offset error for each stage decreases. Resolution of Pipeline ADC can reach 15 bit.

articleTitle: Prism-like effect of nanotubes and nanowires made of noble metals
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The scattering of the H-polarized plane electromagnetic wave by circular gold and silver nanotubes and nanowires with concentric dielectric covers in the visible range of the wavelengths is studied. In each case, the mathematical model is based on the Maxwell equations in the polar coordinates, and the analytical solution of the wave-scattering problem is obtained by the separation of variables. In computations, the complex permittivity of gold or silver is taken from the published experimental data. Unlike previous studies, the focus is on the "prism-like" effect: it is demonstrated that these nanoobjects can scatter specific wavelength bands at different angles.

articleTitle: Optimization of pulse sequence times for signal increasing in diffusion weighted magnetic resonance imaging
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: It is proposed a technique for increasing of the signal to noise ratio for magnetic resonance imaging by selecting the optimum ratio of timing for magnetic resonance pulse sequences. Obtained results show that the using of less value of the pulse duration against the interval time of the pulse sequence gives better result in signal to noise ratio level.

articleTitle: Amplification of optical phonons in semiconductor quantum wells at finite temperatures
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: It is investigated the generation of terahertz radiation with using the oscillations of crystalline lattices. The numerical simulations are presented of the instability of the optical phonons of THz range in the semiconductor structures with quantum wells under the drift of 2D electron gas. The main obstacle for the realization of this instability is the heating of the electron gas. Therefore the low but finite temperatures are considered T ≤ 77 K, and the electron gas is degenerate. In the numerical simulations the kinetic approach is used. It is shown that the structures on the base on GaAs are preferable to observe this instability.

articleTitle: Theoretical investigation of energetic efficiency of impulse high voltage glow discharge electron sources
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: This paper is devoted to the theoretical estimations of energetic efficiency of High Voltage Glow Discharge (HVGD) electron sources in the impulse regime of operation. Balance of energy on the discharge electrodes is analyzed, estimation of energy dissipation in anode plasma is also provided. As a result of investigation obtained the analytical relation for calculation the efficiency of HVGD electron sources. Obtained simulation results are in the good agreement with experimental data.

articleTitle: New microstrip quasi fractal antennas: Design and simulation results
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: New microstrip antennas based on modified versions of Minkowski-like pre-fractal closed loop resonators have been designed in this study as quasi-fractal devices. Both of them have been designed using single layer substrate and dual via ports to operate as multi frequency antennas. The proposed antennas have compact sizes with good radiation performances, which can be adopted in various wireless applications.

articleTitle: Ethanol and water vapors sensing by MIS-structure with porous intermediate layer
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The MIS-type humidity sensor and alcohol - meter based on metal-organic layer-porous silicon (PS) - silicon were elaborated. The influence of the adsorption of ethanol /water mixture on conductivity and capacity voltage (C-V) characteristics was analyzed theoretically and investigated experimentally. The highest response is reached at about 40% concentration of ethanol in water. Such a form of the dependence can be explained by the fact that the adsorption of ethanol and water vapors influences the PS in different ways. The adsorption of donor-type water molecules on the PS surface results in an increase of the conductivity due to the injection of free electrons. The adsorbed on the PS surface the ethanol molecules, on the one hand, prevent the water molecules adsorption and, on the other hand, change the surface recombination rate. The MIS structures with complex dielectric interface (PS + organic layer) show the increased response to the presence of water and ethanol in comparison with structures of metal-PS-Si. To estimate the effect of pores filling/empting on sensors response/recovery time the test PS Bragg mirror was formed and time-depended reflectivity during the adsorption/desorption process was measured.

articleTitle: Modeling of the quantum cascade laser characteristics
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The mathematical model of the quantum cascade structure was proposed for the characteristics analysis of the laser in the terahertz frequency range. Developed model allows to investigate following parameters and characteristics: oscillation frequency, gain frequency characteristics and threshold current density of the super lattice laser heterostructures. The model can be used for optimizing structure and characteristics of the quantum cascade laser (QCL) by the geometrical and electrical parameters.

articleTitle: Peculiarities of the interaction of electromagnetic waves with bio tissue and tool for early diagnosis, prevention and treatment
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: The problem about influence of electromagnetic wave (EMW) on the electron of terminal enzyme of respiratory chain from cytochrome-c-oxidase and other photo acceptors is considered and solved. The solution of problems of encoding and decoding interferogram data and calculation of radiation dose for different spectral composition are proposed. Applied aspects of construction software (SW) of early diagnosis are considered. The results of implementation and testing of SW are discussed for modules such as: calibration of sensitive elements of camera matrix for image analysis; choice of file format for recording, reading and logging; identification of structural elements and determination of the distribution concentration, intensity and spectral composition of radiation dose. The results of testing SW for photodynamic therapy are demonstrated of its efficiency. Experimentally studied and proven that irradiation of muscle by device of resonant conformational photon therapy improves the mechanical properties of the muscles.

articleTitle: A new approach to acoustic beamforming from virtual microphones based on ambisonics for adaptive noise cancelling
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Interference in three-dimensional audio systems is a problematic issue. Eliminating noise, or any other disturbing source, without affecting the spatial audio rendering, is challenging, indeed. Using the least possible number of microphone capsules and reduced size is another issue. An elementary way for accomplishing this job makes use of a 3D audio technique called Ambisonics and a coincident microphone array of 4 elements. This technique allows shaping cardioid-like virtual microphones pointing to a jamming source. This disturbing signal can be used to feed an adaptive noise canceller and kill noise from the 3D recording. Evidently, a 4-capsule array extracts cardioids up to first order. The final result can be improved if microphones with higher directivity are employed. This paper presents a method for deriving highly-directive virtual microphones by means of a 4-capsule ambisonic array and spaced virtual capsules.

articleTitle: Magnetic resonance signal processing tool for diagnostic classification
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Since tissue function has an influence on the structure and integrity, measures that characterize the changes of tissue content allow one to detect the tissue loss or functional damage. The purpose of this investigation is to localize tissue with iron overload and illustrate its simple detection and quantification at magnetic resonance images. This article describes a simple, novel and quantitative method to calculate an ion excess from processing of magnetic resonance signals. After description of iron overload in brain tissues and the magnetic resonance signal processing method the relationships between iron deposition and Alzheimer's disease stages are presented. Magnetic resonance images of independently diagnosed subjects used for assessment of tissue iron. The result of brain tissue iron deposition was the highest in Alzheimer's disease cases and the lowest in normal subjects. Proposed techniques of signal processing allow robust estimates of organ iron concentration with functional correlations in patients with iron overload.

articleTitle: Active dielectrics physics: Modern view
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: Active (or adaptive, or controlled, or smart) dielectrics may easily react to changes of temperature, pressure, mechanical stress, electrical and magnetic fields as well as light illumination. Active dielectrics are classified on the pyroelectrics, ferroelectrics, piezoelectrics, electrets, and on posistor and critistor materials, and others. The nature of sensitive properties of active dielectrics is main topic of report. A number of electrical, mechanical and thermal effects of polar crystals are considered, and the reductive model of crystals internal polarity is proposed.

articleTitle: Microwave dielectrics with unstable electronic spectrum
publicationTitle: 2016 IEEE 36th International Conference on Electronics and Nanotechnology (ELNANO)
abstract: High dielectric constant microwave dielectrics are basic materials for dielectric resonators and filters, as well as for microwave substrates, dielectric waveguides, etc. These dielectrics are possible to improve only through the understanding of physical nature of their polarization. High value E without significant absorption electrical energy at the frequency range of 10…100 GHz can be realized only at the expense of quick-response mechanisms of polarization. The theoretical possibility to obtain thermal stable dielectrics with high εmw but at very low temperatures exists. One previously unknown possibility to combine high permittivity, low loss factor with thermal stability is discussed. It is based on fast-response electronic-phonon mechanism of polarization in dielectrics with the unstable electronic spectrum (like in the quasi one-dimensional crystals of TTF-TCNQ type).
